docs.title: Getting started with custom ERC checks
docs.text: A custom electrical rule check reads an Altium 365 design and reports violations against design objects. Use the Python SDK v1 reference to look up the fields and methods available to a check.

docs.title: Create and test a check
docs.text:
Your organization needs a Custom ERC Checks license. In Admin > Customization > Electrical Rule Checks, select Add and name the check. In the Assigned column, select Assign > Create Script.

Save the script and select Test Run. Enter the ID of the project to check.

Inspect Console for script output and Response for reported violations.

docs.title: Check a required parameter
docs.text:
Suppose your design requires a nonblank Voltage parameter on U1. This script reports the component when the parameter is absent, null or blank. Change the designator to match the component your rule applies to.

from altium_api.v1 import ValidationResult, load_project_data


def onExecute(context, input_parameters):
    project = load_project_data(context, input_parameters)
    result = ValidationResult()
    for component in project.schematic_model.components:
        if component.designator != "U1":
            continue
        has_voltage = any(
            parameter is not None
            and (parameter.name or "").casefold() == "voltage"
            and (parameter.value or "").strip()
            for parameter in component.parameters or ()
        )
        if not has_voltage:
            result.add_violation("U1 requires a Voltage parameter", component)
    return result

The runner calls onExecute and converts the returned ValidationResult to the response dictionary. Attach the relevant component, pin or net to each violation; when nothing matches, return the empty result.

docs.title: Altium API
docs.text:
Use altium_api.v1 to load a design and follow its electrical connections. For reporting rule violations, see Checks. Model classes can be imported from the same namespace or accessed through models:

from altium_api.v1 import DesignData, models

assert DesignData is models.DesignData

docs.title: Project data loading
docs.text:
load_project_data(context, input_parameters) returns a DesignData snapshot. Read components and nets from project.schematic_model, and project metadata, schematics and variants from the root. Pass variantName or variantGuid in the input dictionary to filter the schematic model; the variant catalog stays complete. Use get_project_parameters for project-level name/value pairs.

The model fields below are frozen. Collections are tuples; a required field whose type includes None can still have a null value. Use model_dump() or model_dump_json() to serialize a model.

For connectivity, see Graph navigation. On a loaded project, graph_for(project).net_for(pin) returns a net object or None; pin.net is just its name. Missing or ambiguous IDs do not establish a connection.

docs.title: Graph navigation
docs.text: Call graph_for(project) on a loaded design to traverse connections. pins_for(component) returns its pins; nets_for(component) returns the distinct connected nets. net_for(pin) and component_for(pin) return None when a connection or owner cannot be resolved. variant_for(component) returns the variant name, if present.

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
Use ValidationResult from altium_api.v1 to report what a rule found and which design objects need attention. Create one result per run and return it from onExecute, even when the design passes every check.

from altium_api.v1 import ValidationResult, load_project_data


def onExecute(context, input_parameters):
    project = load_project_data(context, input_parameters)
    result = ValidationResult()
    for component in project.schematic_model.components:
        if not (component.designator or "").strip():
            result.add_violation("Component has no designator", component)
    return result

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
add_violation(violation_reason, obj) attaches a human-readable reason to a v1 component, net, pin, line, net item, or variant. Pass the object itself, not its ID. Unsupported objects raise TypeError.

to_result() groups findings by document and reason. It returns a dictionary whose violations value is a JSON string; an empty result contains "[]". The runner calls this method when you return a ValidationResult.
